feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 9 (score 681) is the best measured design: the same geometry as iteration 8 at base_speed 1.3. The oval stayed at 20 of 20 (max_error 0.016), the s-bend held 18 of 20 finishes with line losses 0.8 and oscillation 0.28, and slalom progress rose from 0.34 to 0.51, though it still has 0 finishes at the 0.064 max_error floor. Iterations 5 to 7 showed mass and body length have reached their useful limit (mass 0.5 reversed the s-bend gain), and iteration 8 showed y 0.075 lifted slalom progress without hurting the oval. That is why the geometry is held fixed here. Read the next race as follows. If slalom progress rises above 0.51 and the s-bend holds 17 or more finishes, speed is still helping, so the geometry can be tested at y 0.08. If the s-bend falls below 17 finishes, the speed cut is costing bend time, so the next geometry trial should be made at base_speed 1.3, not 1.2. If the slalom stays at its max_error floor with 0 finishes at either speed, geometry is the limit and the wheel_track trade is the next test.
requested_changes: If slalom progress rises above 0.51 at base_speed 1.2 and the s-bend holds 17 or more finishes, try sensor y 0.08 (the 0.08 limit) with all other geometry unchanged, since iteration 8 showed y 0.07 to 0.075 lifted slalom progress 0.26 to 0.34 with the oval unchanged.

If the slalom is still at its max_error floor with 0 finishes at base_speed 1.2 or 1.3, try wheel_track 0.095 with y 0.075, since iteration 2 (track 0.10) gave slalom line losses of 1.0 while iteration 3 (track 0.09) gave 1.85 and s-bend progress 0.68, so the track trades s-bend progress against slalom retention.

If the s-bend falls below 17 finishes or its line losses rise above 0.8, keep the geometry fixed and return base_speed to 1.3 (the iteration 9 result), since iteration 7 showed mass changes reverse the s-bend gain and should not be retried.
